title: Jerry Allison: Keep Everything Relatively Simple (Scott K Fish, phone interview 21 March 1982; posted 29 December 2015)
notes: "The kind of music I liked was like Little Richard and Fats Domino"; tried to play like Earl Palmer; Gene Krupa, "I was flipped out with him"; "We use to play the shit out of Bo Diddley at dances"; lessons, learned to read; Peggy Sue: "Basically, that was just paradiddles. Just a basic old rudiment ... Nobody ever asked. We just went ahead and did it"; "We always tried to keep everything relatively simple. That was part of the plan"; "I never did like drum solos".

title: Gary James' Interview With Jerry Allison Of The Crickets (Classic Bands, undated)
notes: Holly had Peggy Sue as a cha-cha or rumba: "I said let's change the beat"; "He and I used to practice all the time"; Premier drums bought in England in 1958, a set made for him; Ludwig later.

title: Jerry Allison, drummer for Buddy Holly, dead at 82 (Kristin M. Hall, Associated Press, 24 August 2022)
notes: Born in Hillsboro, Texas; met Holly in junior high; Peggy Sue, "one of rock's most celebrated drum parts — a rolling pattern called paradiddles"; on Everyday he "ditches the drums and keeps time ... by slapping his knees"; Well... All Right "drumming just on the cymbals"; Rock and Roll Hall of Fame 2012; the last surviving original Crickets member.

title: The Crickets - The "Chirping" Crickets (Brunswick BL 54038, 1957), Discogs release 2152809
notes: Credits: Jerry Allison, drums; Joe Mauldin, bass; Niki Sullivan, guitar; Buddy Holly, lead vocals and guitar. Tracks include Oh, Boy!, Not Fade Away, Maybe Baby and That'll Be the Day.

title: Buddy Holly (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Personnel: the Crickets, Jerry Allison drums; on track 11 (Rave On) Norman Petty piano, Al Caiola and Donald Arnone guitar, five backing singers.

title: Oh, Boy! (The Crickets song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded by the Crickets between 29 June and 1 July 1957 at Norman Petty Studios, the Picks on backing vocals; "an A-A-B-A format with a 12-bar blues verse and an 8-bar bridge".

title: Rave On - Wikipedia
notes: "Produced by Milton DeLugg and recorded with Holly's group the Crickets at Bell Sound Studios in New York City."
